### Language Barrier
Author: Noelle Dey
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/encouragement-cafe/language-barrier-encouragement-caf-june-18-2014.html
Passage: Psalm 109:4
Points:
- Misunderstandings and perceived hostility often stem from hidden insecurities, personal wounds, or communication barriers.
- While it is easy to focus on feeling mistreated in return for love, believers are called to respond with prayer.
- Before allowing offense to take root, ask God to expose and heal any bitterness or brokenness in your own heart.
- Pray for the one who caused offense, choosing compassion over grievance by recognizing they may be acting out of pain.

### Raging Against the Machine? The Surprising Relevance of the Imprecatory Psalms for the Church in an Outrage Culture
Author: Andrew Dunstan
Site: The Gospel Coalition Australia
URL: https://au.thegospelcoalition.org/article/raging-against-the-machine-the-surprising-relevance-of-the-imprecatory-psalms-for-the-church-in-an-outrage-culture/
Passage: Psalm 109:1-31
Points:
- Facing persistent hostility, slander, and persecution naturally stirs up grief and a deep desire for justice.
- Rather than taking vengeance into his own hands, David submitted his raw pain and plea for justice entirely to God in prayer.
- Jesus modeled this same posture under persecution by entrusting Himself fully to the righteous Judge.
- Releasing retribution to God liberates the believer's heart and hands to genuinely love and serve enemies.
- Christians can redirect their outrage toward God by praying for His righteous kingdom to come.
